device.name: Assistive Gym HumanTesting-v1 (PyBullet human arm test)

facts.text: Assistive Gym is a physics-based simulation framework for physical human-robot interaction and robotic assistance
Assistive Gym is integrated into the OpenAI Gym interface
HumanTestingEnv subclasses AssistiveEnv and builds a robot-free world with a controllable human
The controllable human joints are human.right_arm_joints + human.left_arm_joints
right_arm_joints are 0 through 9 and left_arm_joints are 10 through 19
AssistiveEnv builds the action space as a Box with one element per controllable robot and human joint, with every element bounded -1 to 1
HumanTestingEnv passes obs_robot_len=0 and obs_human_len=0 and _get_obs returns an empty list
HumanTestingEnv.step calls take_step with gains 0.05 and forces 1.0 and returns an empty observation, reward 0, done False and an empty info dict
AssistiveEnv defaults time_step to 0.02 s and frame_skip to 5
AssistiveEnv.reset calls p.resetSimulation, disconnects the client and reconnects a DIRECT physics client
AssistiveEnv.reset sets the PyBullet time step to time_step, disables real-time simulation and sets gravity
AssistiveEnv.take_step clips the action to the action space bounds
AssistiveEnv.take_step calls p.stepSimulation frame_skip times per environment step
AssistiveEnv.seed uses gym's seeding.np_random and returns the seed
AssistiveEnv loads realistic_arm_limits_model.h5 from the bundled assets directory

determinism.notes: the reset seed drives gym's numpy generator (env.py:78-80), which picks the human's randomised properties; the exposed observation is the empty list and the reward is always 0, so no value derived from the seed is visible through this interface and every seed gives the same receipts

gaps: PyBullet rigid-body contacts and position-controlled human joints: the motor gains and forces are the constants take_step receives (human_testing.py:16); there is no sensor model, latency model or noise model, so the contract is F1, not F2
the observation is the empty list and the reward is always 0 (human_testing.py:15-20): this is a testing scaffold for the human model, not an assistive task with a task signal
one environment step advances frame_skip=5 physics steps of time_step=0.02 s (env.py:21, :104, :224-226), so the declared 100 ms tick is the environment step, not one PyBullet integration step
the 200-step TimeLimit comes from the Gym registration (assistive_gym/__init__.py:22-26); HumanTestingEnv.step itself always returns done False (human_testing.py:17)
the fake backend does not run PyBullet: it keeps the step counter, the action-space lengths and the 200-step truncation only, and was not compared with the upstream environment
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the simulator needs PyBullet, Keras/TensorFlow, SMPL-X and the bundled asset files (setup.py:21, env.py:37-39), which the gate does not install; no upstream run was performed

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
